candidate_relations.reason: Congenital hydrocephalus is the classic incompatible differential: a cortical mantle is essentially absent here with preserved deep structures.
Dominant optic atrophy does not explain hemispheric replacement by fluid.
A simplified gyral pattern implies residual cortex, conflicting with hydranencephalic destruction.
Marked ventriculomegaly here reflects destroyed hemispheres, not hypertensive hydrocephalus.
Optic-nerve hypoplasia with double-ring sign is an associated ocular finding.
No cobblestone cortex, cobblestone lissencephaly, or muscle-eye-brain features of Walker-Warburg are described.
Congenital disorders of glycosylation are not supported as the MRI diagnosis.
Congenital cerebral anomaly is a broad parent missing hydranencephaly specificity.
Monochorionic twin complications provide etiologic context, not the brain lesion name.
Neurodevelopmental disorder is a functional parent, not hydranencephaly.

case_quality_flags: MRI shows near-absent hemispheric mantle with preserved deep gray matter, brainstem, and cerebellum after co-twin demise
